title: Visualización y comunicación accesible
review_contracts: PYARCANA — MODO REVISOR ESCÉPTICO Y ANTI-COMPLACENCIA
Solarized Website Content Comprehension Auditor & Rewriter

prior_audit.method: Direct fetch of audit/lessons-only/sections/S19.json returned 404 before this audit was created.

learner_entry_state.credit_rule: Only prior concepts marked USABLE count as learned.
learner_entry_state.critical_dependency_warning: S18 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED with 24 material findings. Its confidence-interval baseline, share-as-bias language, bootstrap stability, anomaly-rate denominators, traceability example and data-note provenance cannot be inherited as trustworthy inputs.

roadmap_expectation.T1: Visualización: pregunta/audiencia/selección; ejes y encodings honestos
roadmap_expectation.gate: Cuatro gráficos estáticos y una vista interactiva con conclusión limitada a evidencia y equivalente no visual

live_site.verified_card: S19 · Viz accesible · Cuatro gráficos estáticos y una vista interactiva...
live_site.constraint: The current web fetch exposed the landing-page curriculum card but not the hydrated S19 lesson body. No rendered-only defect is asserted without evidence.

external_benchmarks.principle: Charts/graphs may require a short description plus a longer textual equivalent or structured data representation.
Color cannot be the only visual means of conveying information.

external_benchmarks.source: WCAG 2.2 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus + 2.1.1 Keyboard
external_benchmarks.principle: Custom tooltip-like content must work with keyboard focus and, when applicable, be dismissible, hoverable and persistent.
Chart type follows the relationship/question; bar charts use a zero baseline; line-chart baselines depend on the analytical purpose.
Agg is non-interactive and file output is produced with savefig; metadata alone is not an exported figure.
A quantitative encoding hierarchy is more nuanced than position > length > color > shape; position/common scale and length are strong quantitative channels while hue/shape serve different tasks.

findings.title: S19 opens by treating S18 outputs as already trustworthy
findings.evidence: Opening: 'El EDA de S18 dejó medianas, tamaños de muestra e incertidumbre.'
findings.impact: Learner can chart S18 artifacts whose denominators, intervals, provenance and traceability are still unresolved, laundering upstream uncertainty into polished figures.
findings.repair: Make the handoff conditional: first verify S18 data note, denominator, uncertainty method and exact analytical payload before visualization.

findings.title: Audience guidance is framed as role stereotype rather than task and decision need
findings.evidence: Opening: 'Una gerencia necesita una idea y pocas categorías; un equipo de análisis aguanta más detalle.'
findings.impact: Teaches learners to simplify by job title instead of matching density to decision, time, expertise and consequence.
findings.repair: Define audience by decision, time budget, prior knowledge and required drill-down; role can be an example, not the rule.

findings.title: Encoding hierarchy is materially oversimplified
findings.evidence: T1-B: 'Jerarquía de encodings: posición > longitud > color > forma.'
findings.impact: Conflates quantitative accuracy with categorical channels and omits angle/area distinctions; learner may treat hue or shape as ordered quantitative encodings.
findings.repair: Teach position on common scale and length as strong quantitative channels; distinguish angle/area and explain that hue/shape are primarily categorical, not a universal numeric ranking.

findings.title: The claimed visual-inflation factor is never calculated
findings.evidence: T1-B says calculate '(altura_truco / altura_honesta)'; code prints 0.67 and 0.10 separately. Their ratio, the actual inflation factor under that definition, is 6.67.
findings.impact: A central integrity gate appears executable but does not produce the metric named by the prose.
findings.repair: Define the metric precisely and print `factor_inflacion = ratio_truco / ratio_honesto` (=6.67 for the fixture), while explaining what the ratio represents and its limits.

findings.title: Matplotlib outcome promises bar-count verification but the canonical theory example omits it
findings.evidence: Outcome and T2-A prose name 'n de barras' / 'conteo de barras'; `mpl_bar.py` records axes/ylabel/ylim only.
findings.impact: The learner sees a stated executable contract that the worked example does not actually demonstrate.
findings.repair: Capture the returned BarContainer or inspect `ax.patches` and assert/print the expected number of bars.

findings.title: The multi-panel example silently applies the bar zero-baseline rule to a line chart
findings.evidence: T2-B loops over both axes and runs `ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)`, including the panel titled 'Tendencia'.
findings.impact: Learner may generalize 'all Y axes start at zero', although the section correctly scopes the strict zero rule to bar-length magnitude encodings.
findings.repair: Apply zero baseline to the bar panel only; teach line-axis choice from analytical purpose and provide sufficient contextual scale.

findings.title: Export contract says savefig is required while the code only simulates metadata
findings.evidence: T2-B: 'Exporta de verdad con fig.savefig'; code comment says '# simular export metadata' and never calls savefig.
findings.impact: The exact skill named in the learning outcome—producing a versioned PNG—is not demonstrated, and a metadata dict can pass while no artifact exists.
findings.repair: Write to BytesIO or a temporary/versioned file with `fig.savefig(..., dpi=120, bbox_inches='tight')`; validate non-zero bytes/format and derive metadata from the created artifact.

findings.title: Migration from a data spec to Plotly/Streamlit is called 'mechanical'
findings.evidence: T3-A and callout: 'si el modelo es claro, migrar a una librería interactiva es mecánico.'
findings.impact: Hides real work in event/state semantics, accessibility, keyboard behavior, responsiveness and library-specific rendering.
findings.repair: Say the spec reduces migration ambiguity but implementation still requires library-specific interaction and accessibility validation.

findings.title: Interactive accessibility contract omits keyboard/focus and tooltip behavior
findings.evidence: T3-A minimal spec is `{filtro, tooltip_template, unidad, campos_visibles}` and discusses hover/tooltips but not keyboard focus, focus order, dismissibility, hoverability or persistence.
findings.impact: A dashboard can satisfy the lesson's spec while remaining unusable to keyboard and screen-reader users; this conflicts with the section's central accessibility claim.
findings.repair: Extend the spec with keyboard-reachable controls, focus-visible behavior, accessible names/state, tooltip trigger by focus as well as pointer, and WCAG 1.4.13 behavior when custom hover/focus content is used.

findings.title: Filter-driven conclusion recalculation and JSON state serialization are promised but not demonstrated
findings.evidence: T3-A contract requires recalculating conclusion and serializing state; `interactive_spec.py` only filters one row and prints a tooltip dict.
findings.impact: The example does not test the product defect the paragraph warns about, so a stale global conclusion would still pass.
findings.repair: Build a serializable state object, derive the filtered summary/conclusion from `vista`, serialize it with JSON, and test a second filter where the leader/conclusion changes.

findings.title: Active filter says Lima while accessible table and chart value describe Madrid
findings.evidence: T3-B code: `state['filtro_region']='Lima'`, while `alt_table[0]['region']='Madrid'` and `chart_value=28.0` matches the Madrid row.
findings.impact: The canonical accessibility example violates its own filtered-state parity contract.
findings.repair: Generate chart value, table row, alt text and sample metadata from the same filtered payload/state.

findings.title: The parity check is a one-scalar false positive
findings.evidence: `match = chart_value == alt_table[0]['ticket_mediano_pen']` prints True despite the Lima/Madrid state contradiction.
findings.impact: Learner is explicitly shown a green integrity gate that misses row identity, active filter, categories, n and precision—the failure modes the section claims to prevent.
findings.repair: Compare normalized chart-data and table-data records including key/category, metric, value, n, filter state and display precision; fail on missing/extra rows.

findings.title: Viewport sampling n and metric n are presented without distinct definitions
findings.evidence: T3-B state contains sample_n=5000/universe_n=50000 while the accessible row independently says n=40.
findings.impact: Learner cannot tell whether n means rendered points, analytical observations behind a statistic, or population coverage.
findings.repair: Name each denominator explicitly, e.g. `rendered_points_n`, `eligible_universe_n`, `metric_observations_n`, and state their relationship.

findings.title: The 'accessible table' contract stops at numeric parity and omits table semantics
findings.evidence: T3-B defines 'alternativa accesible = tabla ordenable + resumen textual' but never states headers/caption/row-column associations or keyboard-operable sorting.
findings.impact: A visually tabular or mouse-only sortable component could satisfy the prose yet remain inaccessible to assistive technology.
findings.repair: Add programmatic headers/caption and keyboard-operable sort-state requirements to the contract; numeric parity is necessary but not sufficient.

findings.title: Caption provenance is manually authored rather than bound to the analytical payload
findings.evidence: T4-A hardcodes source, cutoff, n and limitation in a dict; no dataset/data-note identifier, hash or derivation is checked.
findings.impact: A polished caption can drift away from the data it describes, especially because S18's data-note example is itself unresolved.
findings.repair: Build caption metadata from the validated S18 note/payload identity and carry a stable data-note or payload identifier into the figure manifest.

findings.title: 'Contraste suficiente' is not operationalized
findings.evidence: T4-B says 'Contraste suficiente texto/fondo' but gives no measurable threshold and does not distinguish text from graphical-object contrast.
findings.impact: Learner cannot test the requirement; subjective 'se ve bien' can pass despite WCAG failures.
findings.repair: Teach the relevant WCAG targets for normal/large text and required non-text graphical information, while preserving the non-color channel rule.

findings.title: Final alt text and the supposedly acceptable claim disagree about which region leads
findings.evidence: `alt` says Lima 28, Madrid 24, Bogota 22.5; `claim_ok` says Madrid has the highest median.
findings.impact: The section closes its no-overclaim lesson with a claim contradicted by its own evidence.
findings.repair: Derive the claim from the same rows used to build the alt/table; with the shown values the permitted claim must say Lima leads the sample.

findings.title: The nominal Peru case mixes Lima with Madrid, Bogota and Berlin as if they were peer Peruvian regions
findings.evidence: Job relevance warns against 'Madrid lidera el Perú'; examples repeatedly label a Peru case while using Madrid/Bogota/Berlin alongside Lima.
findings.impact: Breaks the localized mental model and makes population/generalization statements geographically incoherent.
findings.repair: Either use Peruvian peer geographies consistently (e.g. Lima/Arequipa/Trujillo) or explicitly define a multinational market dimension and stop saying 'del Perú'.

findings.title: T4-B contains an unscaffolded SQL/ML-leakage mini-lesson outside S19's roadmap
findings.evidence: After three accessibility/claims paragraphs, four additional paragraphs introduce Codd/SEQUEL, SQL fundamentals, sqlite3 and ML leakage. S19 roadmap assigns T4-B to color/contrast/alt/no-overclaim; SQL was already S12 and leakage has a later dedicated progression.
findings.impact: Adds cognitive load at the exact closure point, weakens narrative coherence and displaces practice on the section's actual accessibility gate.
findings.repair: Remove this detour from S19 theory or reduce it to a one-sentence provenance bridge; keep SQL teaching in its owning section and leakage in its dedicated ML progression.

findings.title: The leakage paragraph falsely says the learner saw ML Pipeline behavior in S09
findings.evidence: T4-B: 'En ML (como viste en S09)...'; current S09 canonical title is 'Excepciones, debugging y logging seguro'.
findings.impact: Creates a nonexistent prerequisite and leaves a zero-tech learner without the background the paragraph assumes.
findings.repair: Delete the S09 reference; if the material remains, introduce it self-sufficiently or point only to the actual later ML/leakage owner.

findings.title: 'Describe con todo' is unsafe guidance for a held-out test set
findings.evidence: T4-B rule: 'describe con todo, decide solo con lo que verías en producción.'
findings.impact: Inspecting a held-out test set during exploratory analysis can influence feature/model/threshold decisions and leak test information even without fit_transform.
findings.repair: Keep the final test set sealed from model-development EDA; explore train/development data, make decisions there, then use the test set only for the predeclared final evaluation.

findings.title: SQL detour presents an overly categorical 'four fundamental operations' model
findings.evidence: T4-B: 'Las cuatro operaciones fundamentales de SQL son SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY y JOIN.'
findings.impact: Conflates clauses/operations and presents a narrow dashboard-query subset as the fundamentals of SQL.
findings.repair: If retained, call them four common clauses/operations for analytical SELECT queries, not the four fundamentals of SQL.

findings.title: SQL example defaults to AVG(ticket) without reconnecting to S18's robust-metric decision
findings.evidence: The detour's example uses `AVG(ticket)` immediately after S18 taught that skewed ticket values can make mean a poor 'typical' metric.
findings.impact: Learner can infer that the SQL layer licenses a different metric simply because AVG is convenient.
findings.repair: Tie the aggregation to the stated business question; if mean is used, say why. Otherwise show that robust metrics may require a different query/processing path.

findings.title: Spanish-first redaction is weakened by a dense cluster of unexplained or inconsistently translated terms
findings.evidence: Examples include chart, brief, encoding, dual-axis, faceting, state, sample, aggregate, claim, loop, gate, metadata and portfolio; T4-B also contains 'cambiaria' without the required accent 'cambiaría'.
findings.impact: Raises unnecessary lexical load for a zero-tech learner and breaks the course's self-sufficient Peruvian-Spanish contract.
findings.repair: Introduce Spanish first with the English term only where useful, reuse one stable translation, and correct grammar/accents.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: All non-zero chart axes are deceptive.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: The strict zero-baseline requirement is appropriate for bar-length magnitude encodings; line charts require contextual scale choices rather than a universal zero rule.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: Using the Agg backend is obsolete or incorrect.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: Current Matplotlib documentation still identifies Agg as a non-interactive raster backend suitable for file generation.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: A separate data table makes alt text unnecessary in every case.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: Complex-image guidance supports a short identification/summary plus a longer textual/data equivalent; responsibilities depend on context.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: Any use of color in a chart is inaccessible.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: WCAG prohibits color as the only information channel; color may be used with redundant text/pattern/position and adequate contrast.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: The source header comment is a learner-facing meta leak.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: It is source-only TypeScript commentary; current text fetch did not establish that it is rendered to learners.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: The figure alt 'Cuatro guardas...' is definitely insufficient.
rejected_hypotheses.reason: The current tooling did not expose the hydrated figure, so its informational dependence on the image versus surrounding text cannot be proven.

source_only_notes: File header explains legacy filename/id and warns agents not to match content to slug. This is developer-facing source commentary and is not counted as a learner-facing leak without render evidence.

strengths_defended: Zero-baseline discipline for bars is correct.
Chart/table numerical parity is the right concept even though the canonical test is inadequate.
No-overclaim language correctly inherits S18's association/decision caution in principle.
pedagogical_deep_dive.dominant_failure_pattern: The prose states strong executable contracts, but several canonical examples do not execute the contract they name. This creates false-green pedagogy: the learner sees a passing example that would miss the very defect the text warns about.
pedagogical_deep_dive.cognitive_load: The late SQL/ML-leakage detour is the largest sequencing violation. It introduces a second domain just as the learner should consolidate accessibility, provenance and evidence-limited communication.
pedagogical_deep_dive.accessibility_gap: The section emphasizes non-visual equivalents but under-specifies interactive operability: keyboard/focus, tooltip persistence/dismissal and programmatic table semantics remain outside the executable contract.

priority_order: P1 first: F11/F12/F17 — repair false-green parity and claim/data contradictions.
P1: F07/F05/F04/F10 — make export, bar-count, inflation and filter/conclusion contracts actually executable.
P1: F09 — extend accessibility from visual redundancy to keyboard/focus/tooltip behavior.
P1: F01/F15 — bind S19 figures to a validated S18 analytical payload and provenance note.
P1: F18/F19/F20/F21 — remove geography incoherence and the SQL/ML scope/prerequisite/leakage defects.
P2: F03/F06/F08/F13/F14/F16/F22/F23/F24 — refine perception, axis, terminology, denominator and WCAG details.

USABLE: bar length magnitude comparisons use a zero baseline
color must not be the sole information channel
figure claims must not exceed evidence
Agg can support headless static rendering
MISCONCEPTION_RISK: all chart axes should start at zero
sample_n and metric n are interchangeable
Madrid/Bogota/Berlin are peer regions in a Peru population claim
S09 taught ML Pipeline leakage controls
held-out test data are safe for unrestricted descriptive EDA during model development
S20_watchlist: Do not consume S19 figure metadata as proof a PNG exists unless artifact bytes/file are verified.
Do not trust S19 chart-table parity unless key/category/value/n/filter/precision are reconciled, not one scalar.
Carry explicit denominator names into Excel outputs.
Do not inherit the Lima/Madrid geography fixtures.
Keep S18/S19 provenance unresolved until captions bind to the validated analytical payload.
